newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Industrivarden says '96 profit down, dividend up.
newsitem.headline: Industrivarden says '96 profit down, dividend up.

text.p: Swedish holding company Industrivarden said on Tuesday its 1996 profit after financial items fell 20 percent to 1.42 billion crowns ($186.6 million), but still proposed to raise dividends by two crowns to 13 crowns a share.
The profit was hurt by a fall in sales to 5.55 billion crowns from 5.89 billion crowns in 1995.
However the company said, if calculated at a fixed foreign exchange rate, sales rose by about six percent over the 12 months to December 31, 1996.
The share of sales abroad rose to 68 percent from 67 percent.

The profit included gains of shares sold amounting to 679 million crowns against 86 million crowns in 1995, and a 508 million crown capital gain deriving from the sale of Industrivarden's 22 percent stake in beverage packaging group PLM.
In 1995, the profit included a one off gain of 1.2 billion crowns stemming from the sale of 55 percent of shares in PLM.

On the positive side, the company's net asset value (NAV) rose to 455 crowns a share at the end of 1996 from 333 crowns at the end of 1995. On February 28 1997, net asset value amounted to 501 crowns, the company said.
Also, net financial items narrowed to a 121 million crown charge, from a charge of 258 million crowns.
The value of Industrivarden's bourse portfolio rose to 17.75 billion crowns at the end of 1996 from 13.78 billion crowns a year earlier, the company said.
"Adjusted for acquisitions and sales, the bourse portfolio value rose during the year by 36 percent (compared to 20 percent a year earlier)," Industrivarden said in a statement.
Still, the portfolio underperformed the Stockholm Stock Exchange's general index, which rose 38 percent in 1996 and 18 percent in 1995.
During the year, the company acquired shares for 563 million crowns, compared to 820 million a year earlier.
The company acquired shares in insurance company Skandia, drugs major Astra and holding company Custos.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.609 Swedish Crowns)
